headline: Dexory's cost of adding a new Integrity class scales with the number of daily scans rather than with what the model actually learns, and curation plus per-site model evaluation is where that breaks.
what_they_build: Autonomous scanning robots drive warehouse aisles daily and turn scan data into DexoryView: real-time inventory accuracy, plus Integrity (inventory discrepancies, hygiene or damage risks, rack compliance) and Optimise (slotting, space utilisation, consolidation). Buyers are 3PLs and manufacturers such as Ziegler, Romark Logistics, Seac and Stellantis, on a monthly per-site subscription, roughly $28.6m est. ARR.
inferred_pipeline: Robot runs a scheduled mission per aisle, capturing camera imagery plus LIDAR and barcode or RFID reads with pose and location metadata (mission scheduling confirmed by site; sensor mix is our guess).
Scans upload to cloud object storage and are keyed to site, aisle, rack and location; volumes are millions of near-identical shelf frames per site per week (our guess on scale).
Perception models read location contents, barcodes and empties, and Integrity models flag damage, hygiene and rack compliance; discrepancies are reconciled against the customer's WMS.
Labelling for new classes such as damaged stock or leaning pallets is likely a mix of internal review and an outsourced or managed workforce, driven by whatever frames look interesting (guess).

Operational and perception signals land in a lakehouse: the Senior Data Engineer ad names Databricks, perception accuracy, scan and mission performance, obstructions and scan coverage against per-site SLAs.
Model performance is reported per site in dashboards; failure analysis by scene condition or class slice is probably manual (guess).

hypotheses.pain: Daily repeat scans of the same racking mean labelling budget buys mostly duplicates, so cost grows with fleet and site count instead of with model accuracy.
hypotheses.evidence: Site text: automated daily scans, scale across multiple sites without disruption; our note on millions of near-identical shelf images per site per week.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Index registers the frames in Dexory's own bucket, computes embeddings and per-frame metrics (sharpness, brightness, uniqueness), then similarity search and diversity sampling build a Collection to label. Our warehouse-robot benchmark cut frames to label by 61% keeping 95% of racks.

hypotheses.pain: New Integrity classes like damaged stock, leaning pallets and hygiene risks are rare, subjective and expensive to bootstrap, so early label quality and class definitions drift between annotators.
hypotheses.evidence: Storage Health launched Feb 2026; site text lists damage risks and rack compliance under the Integrity module as ML-flagged outputs.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Annotate ontology with objects plus attributes pins the definition of damaged versus leaning versus non-compliant; SAM 3 and object tracking across video speed up masks; Agents run a Dexory model or foundation model as a pre-label stage; Active finds label errors.

hypotheses.pain: Per-site perception accuracy is reported but not diagnosable: no easy way to see which conditions (blur, low light, obstruction, rack type) drive misses, or what to label next.
hypotheses.evidence: Job ad: model perception accuracy, scan and mission performance, obstructions and scan coverage against SLAs and KPIs we have committed to per site.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Active imports Dexory predictions and gives mAP/mAR/F1, PR curves and confusion matrix sliced by class, IoU threshold and any data metric; metric-to-failure correlation names the data slice to label next. Outputs can feed the Databricks layer via SDK.

ontology.name: Pallet in location
ontology.why: Core unit for occupancy and WMS discrepancy checks

ontology.name: Empty location
ontology.why: Drives inventory accuracy and slotting or consolidation suggestions

ontology.name: Barcode or location placard
ontology.why: Small, skewed text regions; box wastes pixels on angled labels

ontology.name: Damaged stock or packaging
ontology.why: Damage is irregular; mask supports severity attributes for Integrity

ontology.name: Leaning or overhanging pallet
ontology.why: Lean and aisle intrusion need orientation, not an axis-aligned box

ontology.name: Rack beam and upright
ontology.why: Rack compliance and deflection checks follow long thin structures

ontology.name: Aisle obstruction or debris
ontology.why: Job ad names obstructions as an SLA signal; shapes vary widely

ontology.name: Scan quality flag (blur, low light, occluded)
ontology.why: Lets Active slice accuracy by condition and gates curation

case_study.name: Automotus, plus Encord's own warehouse-robot curation benchmark
case_study.why_it_matches: Automotus runs fixed street cameras producing huge volumes of highly repetitive frames, the same redundancy problem as daily rack scans; curation, not more labels, moved accuracy. Our internal shelf-image benchmark is the closest direct analogue to Dexory's aisle passes.
case_study.numbers: Automotus: +20% mAP, 35% smaller dataset, 33% lower labelling cost. Warehouse-robot benchmark: 61% fewer frames to label keeping 95% of racks, YOLOv8n 0.48 vs 0.43 mAP50 against a random pick of equal size.

proof_of_value: Week 0: register one site's recent scans from Dexory's existing S3/GCS bucket in Index (data never moves), agree the slice: one or two sites, one or two weeks of scans, plus the current Storage Health class list.

Week 1: generate embeddings and quality metrics, de-duplicate the repeat aisle passes and build two equal-sized Collections, curated versus random. Success metric: percentage reduction in frames needed to retain agreed rack or location coverage.

Week 1: import existing predictions for pallet, empty location and one Integrity class into Active; produce confusion matrix and accuracy sliced by blur, brightness and obstruction per site. Success metric: at least three named failure slices Dexory did not have visibility on.

Week 2: label the curated Collection in Annotate with the agreed ontology, using SAM 3 and tracking, and run an Agents pre-label stage on the damage class. Success metric: minutes per frame versus current baseline, plus reviewer agreement on the new classes.

Week 2: retrain or fine-tune on curated versus random picks of equal size and compare in Active. Success metric: mAP or F1 delta on a held-out site, and a cost-per-usable-label figure to take to the CFO.
Exit: SDK script that pushes Encord metrics into the Databricks layer so perception accuracy per site sits alongside the SLA tables.
discovery_questions: When you added the Storage Health classes, how many frames did you label to get the first usable model, and how did you choose those frames out of the daily scans?
Across a week of scans at one site, what proportion do you actually keep for training, and what decides that today?
When a site misses its perception accuracy SLA, how long does it take to find out whether it is lighting, blur, obstruction, rack type or a genuine model gap?
Who labels today: internal ops reviewers, an outsourced vendor, or a tool your team built, and what is the per-class cost of that?
The Senior Data Engineer ad mentions modelling perception accuracy against per-site SLAs in Databricks. Is that metric currently produced by the perception team by hand?
risks: Strong build instinct: they are hiring a founding data engineer on Databricks and may treat curation and evaluation as internal platform work rather than a bought tool.
The evidence is about business and SLA data, not labelling pain; no perception or annotation job ad, so the hypotheses are inferred rather than observed.
Data access and security review: customer warehouse imagery under contract, so expect SOC2, GDPR and per-customer consent hurdles before a POV on real scans.

Cost discipline signals (CFO profile, subscription model, ROI calculator) mean any tool spend must map to labelling cost per site, and a cheaper incumbent (Roboflow, V7, a BPO with its own tool) may be good enough.
